ticket.title: Add a schema-configurable searchable dropdown backed by a live REST endpoint
ticket.text:
Add a schema-configurable searchable dropdown backed by a live REST endpoint

# The problem

A nurse fills in an insurance claim form on behalf of the treating doctor. The claim has to identify the clinician, and the list of eligible clinicians lives in an insurer-maintained directory that changes continuously — people join, leave, and lose accreditation.

Today our forms can't do this well:

- Static dropdown choices are fixed when the form is built, so they go stale
- Remote choices already exist (remote-select), but each list source must be registered in application code, so connecting a form to a new live list needs a developer and a software release
- The first attempt ([PR reference removed], superseded) downloaded the whole list in one request — big lists get cut off, there's no real search, and reopened forms show a code instead of a name. [PR reference removed] is the active implementation.

# What we'd build

A built-in data source that a form schema can point at a REST endpoint, so form builders can back any dropdown with a live list without engine or host-app code changes.

# Acceptance criteria

1. Typing sends the entered term through the configured search parameter and displays matching results.
2. Each result displays its `labelKey` value; selecting it returns the `valueKey` value to the existing form control and adapter (an obs question stores it as the obs value, exactly as any select does today).
3. The initial (empty-term) load requests a bounded page (`limit`, default 20, overridable) — never the full collection.
4. Reopening a saved form resolves the stored value and displays its label.
5. The field works correctly inside existing repeating groups, with independent search and edit-mode resolution for every row. (Repetition itself is the existing repeating mechanism, not this feature.)
6. Search and resolution failures produce a visible, accessible error state distinguishable from "no matches." Note: today's remote-select collapses errors into an empty list for every data source, so this is a shared-behavior enhancement in the control as well as a data-source requirement — see the implementation contract.
7. Existing forms and registered data sources behave unchanged, and the library gains no new required provider for consumers (`HttpClient` must remain optional — consumers that don't provide it keep working, minus this data source).
8. Focused tests cover option mapping (`results`-wrapped and bare-array responses), search parameter construction, saved-value resolution, search and resolution failures versus successful empty results (including the visible error state), and the registration/compatibility guarantees in criterion 7.

# Implementation contract

- Configuration uses the standard `questionOptions.datasource: { name, config }` schema key and renders through the existing `remote-select` control. A parallel rendering type or schema key does not satisfy this ticket.
- The engine registers the data source itself (working name `endpoint`) in the shared `DataSources` registry via optional injection, and only when that name is not already registered. A host-provided implementation therefore takes precedence regardless of initialization order: if the host registered first, the engine defers (the guard); if the host registers later, the registry's existing last-registration-wins overwrite applies. Both directions are test-pinned.
- Config keys: `endpointUrl` (required), `labelKey` (default `display`), `valueKey` (default `uuid`), `searchParam` (default `q`), `resultsKey` (default `results`), `limit` (default `20`), `limitParam` (default `limit`).
- Saved-value resolution convention: `GET {endpointUrl}/{urlEncodedValue}`, overridable via an optional `resolveUrlTemplate` config with a `{value}` placeholder.
- The endpoint data source must not convert request failures into an empty successful result; failures propagate to the control. Remote-select distinguishes a request failure from a successful empty response and exposes an accessible error message.
- Supported endpoints are browser-accessible HTTP GET endpoints returning JSON (a `results`-wrapped or bare array). Custom authentication is out of scope: same-origin endpoints may use the existing session; cross-origin endpoints must already be browser-accessible with suitable CORS configuration. Relative URLs are the portability norm (to be documented). GraphQL and POST search are out of scope.

# Where the selection is stored — answered

The earlier open questions to the implementing team have been resolved, and the DHA HIE docs corrected two premises:

- All selectable clinicians exist as OpenMRS providers; the form stores the provider UUID.
- Regulator details (licence number, licensing body) live as provider attributes synced from the registry; the claim resolves them at build time — a standard claim identifies exactly one doctor by `practitioner_identification_number` + `practitioner_regulation_body`.
- Doctor approval exists only for emergency (ECCIF) claims and is run by the HIE via OTP; standard claims have no approval step.

None of that changes this ticket's mechanism — it's recorded so the claims form design consuming this feature doesn't re-open it.

# Not in scope

- The encounter-provider enhancements (multiple providers, configurable roles) — separate ticket; this feature is its search mechanism
- The eligible-providers endpoint and licence re-validation at claim build — claims module
- Claim generation or submission
- The React form engine equivalent
